equity_bridge.note: Book equity 6,953 at 2 Aug 2026 (Q3 FY2026 10-Q supplemental consolidating balance sheet). Residual income: sustainable ROE ~11.5% (FY2023-FY2026E range 9.5%-12.4%; FY2026 net income guided ~870), growth 3%, cost of equity 10% -> P/B (11.5-3)/(10-3) = 1.21x. Held at the base value in all three scenarios because the bridge is not scenario-specific; a 1.0x-1.4x range is worth roughly -5/+5 per share.
Equipment operations' cash lent to the captive (Q3 FY2026 10-Q, 'Receivables from Financial Services'); already a liability inside Financial Services book equity, interest excluded from the flows.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case 10-year net sales CAGR from the FY2026E trough (cycle-normalised); equity CAGR rejected, see warning
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-yr CAGR (14.9%) diverges by far more than 30% from revenue (5.2%) and the 3-yr figures are negative for revenue, EPS and FCF: FY2020 was a trough and FY2023 a record peak, so every trailing CAGR is a statement about cycle position, not trend. None is used as the growth driver.
historical_growth.notes: Revenue, EPS and equity are consolidated FY2025 vs FY2022 / FY2020. FCF CAGR is on the EQUIPMENT OPERATIONS owner-FCF series (EO operating cash flow less Financial Services dividends less capex less SBC less interest income ex-FS): FY2021 4,336, FY2022 4,420, FY2023 9,521, FY2024 4,319, FY2025 1,803. The 5-yr figure is null because the FY2020 supplemental consolidating cash flow is not in the filings on hand (4-yr FY2021-FY2025: -19.7%). Reported EO FCF 3-yr CAGR is -20.2% (4,664 -> 2,374); the owner series falls faster because interest income ex-FS rose from 159 to 420 and SBC from 85 to 151. Consolidated FCF in the Metrics CSV is not meaningful: Financial Services receivable originations sit in investing activities.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2026 is the large-ag trough, as management says. Used high-horsepower inventory (down ~40% YoY) clears, PPA recovers from FY2027 while Construction & Forestry and Small Ag & Turf growth normalises from this year's double digits; net sales regain the FY2023 nominal peak of ~$55bn around FY2031 and then grow with inflation plus modest precision-ag content. Margins rebuild from ~12.5% EBIT to a mid-cycle ~15.3% (19% adjusted EBITDA): better than every pre-2021 cycle because of pricing and structural cost work, but short of the 20% Leap Ambition because tariffs stay a net cost, precision-ag subscriptions monetise slowly and the 10-year right-to-repair consent decree trims some aftermarket parts and service profit. Financial Services earns ~11.5% on equity.
scenario_narratives.bull: A proper ag upcycle: replacement demand after three years of under-buying, lower rates and firmer farm income drive net sales ~$50bn by FY2028 and ~$63bn by FY2031, with Construction & Forestry sustained by infrastructure, data-centre and rental-fleet spend. See & Spray, autonomy and Operations Center subscriptions lift mix, tariff recoveries continue, and Deere holds an ~18.5% EBIT margin (22% adjusted EBITDA) through the cycle - close to its own 20% target, and still below the 21% it printed at the FY2023 peak. This needs both the cycle and the technology monetisation to deliver.
scenario_narratives.bear: FY2026 is not the trough but the new normal. Farm income stays depressed on low crop prices, high input costs and retaliatory tariffs against US-built equipment; South America and Europe keep softening; the construction boost from data centres and rental fleets fades. Net sales grow only ~2-3% a year from $41.6bn. EBIT margin stays near today's ~12.4% (16% adjusted EBITDA) as tariffs remain a ~$0.5bn net cost, incentives stay elevated to move used equipment, and the consent decree erodes dealer-controlled parts and service. Financial Services credit losses rise but the captive remains worth about book. The business stays solidly cash-generative on this path - the terminal value does not approach the zero floor.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Deere is two businesses: a cyclical equipment manufacturer valued on unlevered, SBC-expensed owner FCF built from mid-cycle margins, and a highly levered captive lender valued on book equity. Summing them avoids treating $54bn of finance-company funding as net debt. The valuation capitalises mid-cycle, not peak, economics at a 15x terminal cap suited to a high-quality cyclical. The market price capitalises something close to the FY2023 peak as a sustainable run-rate.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cycle position: FY0 is an estimated trough year; if FY2026 is not the bottom the base growth path is too high, and if the upcycle is sharp the base is too low. Terminal-year margin (19% adjusted EBITDA) is the single most sensitive driver - each 1pt is worth roughly $20/share.
FY2026E base revenue (41,600) is an estimate built from 9M actuals and the net income guide; actuals were not yet reported at the valuation date.

Cash conversion: equipment operations' actual FCF ran ~7% below the component build over FY2023-FY2025 (pension contributions, accrual unwinds, cash taxes above provision), and far below it in FY2025 alone.

Financial Services is held at 1.2x book in every scenario; a credit cycle in ag lending would hit both the captive's value and equipment demand at the same time, so the bear case modestly understates the correlation.
Terminal cap of 15x binds in all scenarios (Gordon at 9.0%/2.5% is 15.8x); a market that keeps paying 20x+ mid-cycle earnings for Deere would make every scenario look low.
Net pension/OPEB overfunding (~$1.9bn) and its non-cash income are excluded from both bridge and flows.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular session close); 52-week range 455.91-721.22
data_sources.financials: FY2023-FY2025 10-K and Q3 FY2026 10-Q supplemental consolidating data (equipment operations vs Financial Services income statements, balance sheets, cash flows) and segment operating profit reconciliations in research/DE/Extracted; DE_Metrics.csv and the kpis table for consolidated history and segment series
data_sources.qualitative: research/DE/Reports/DE_Analysis.json (2026-11-15): FY2026 guidance as raised at Q3 (net income $4.75-5.0bn, equipment operations operating cash flow $5.0-5.5bn, Financial Services net income ~$870m, capex ~$1.3bn), tariff, consent-decree and cycle commentary

inputs.share_count_basis: 269.625m shares outstanding at 2 Aug 2026 (Q3 FY2026 10-Q cover) plus 0.9m dilutive options/RSUs (Q3 EPS note) = 270.5m fully diluted. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows, and Deere funds the flat count with buybacks.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K consolidated cash flow statement, share-based compensation expense $151m (9M FY2026: $116m). Deere publishes no combined SBC-plus-withholding-tax figure and the withholding line is not separately disclosed; the forward path is set at 0.40% of net sales, slightly above the 0.37-0.39% actual, to cover it.
inputs.fiscal_year_end: Sunday nearest 31 October (FY2026 ended 1 Nov 2026; FY2025 was a 53-week year ended 2 Nov 2025)
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. Risk-free ~4.3% (10-yr UST) + 5.0% ERP x beta ~1.0 = ~9.3% cost of equity; equipment operations carry little net debt (A-rated), so WACC is set at 9.0%. The same 9.0% is used in all three scenarios: cyclicality, tariff and consent-decree risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not in the rate. Financial Services is valued separately at a 10% cost of equity.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases: rent is already an operating expense inside segment operating profit, so no lease adjustment is made and lease liabilities (~$314m at FY2025) are excluded from net debt. Financial Services' equipment on operating leases is a lending asset and sits inside the Financial Services equity value.
inputs.nci_treatment: Immaterial. Redeemable noncontrolling interest of $44m deducted in the equity bridge; the $7m of other NCI and the ~$6m/yr NCI loss are ignored.
inputs.net_debt_note: EQUIPMENT OPERATIONS ONLY, from the supplemental consolidating balance sheet at 2 Aug 2026: borrowings 417 + 1 + 8,907 = 9,325; cash 6,607 + marketable securities 155 = 6,762. Financial Services' $54.5bn of borrowings are operating funding for the receivable book and are NOT net debt; they are netted inside the Financial Services equity value in the bridge. The CSV's consolidated total_debt column (short-term borrowings only since Q3 2022) is not used.
inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026E equipment operations NET SALES (excludes finance income and Financial Services revenue): 9M actual 30,779 (+8.6% YoY) plus Q4 estimated ~10,800 against 10,579 in the 14-week Q4 FY2025, consistent with the raised FY2026 net income guide of $4.75-5.0bn (implies Q4 net income 0.94-1.19bn vs 1.07bn). FY2025 actual net sales were 38,917. FY2026 results had not been reported at the valuation date; replace this estimate with the actual when the 10-K lands (late Nov / Dec 2026).
inputs.last_fcf_note: last_fcf and reported_fcf are the latest ACTUAL year (FY2025), equipment operations only: EO operating cash flow 5,100 less 1,368 dividends received from Financial Services less 1,358 capex = 2,374 reported; less SBC 151 and interest income ex-FS 420 = 1,803 owner FCF. This figure is after 372 of EO interest expense and was depressed by 814 of largely voluntary pension contributions and a 617 unwind of payables/incentive accruals in the downturn. The forward build does not compound from it; it is rebuilt from components off FY2026E net sales.
inputs.notes: MODEL: sum of the parts, run through the owner-FCF component engine. Deere straddles two rows of the dcf-methods routing table, so the parts are valued separately and summed. (1) Equipment Operations (PPA, SAT, CF plus corporate) = cyclical operating company -> owner-FCF DCF with the cyclical adaptations; flows are unlevered, SBC-expensed, built off net sales and segment operating profit less corporate-other, excluding all interest income, Financial Services dividends and the non-cash pension/OPEB benefit. (2) Financial Services (John Deere Capital etc.) = captive lender at 8.6x debt/equity -> residual-income P/B on book equity at a 10% cost of equity, added in the equity bridge; a consolidated owner-FCF would treat $54bn of funding debt as net debt and receivable originations as cash burn, which is meaningless. (3) The $5.4bn intercompany receivable from Financial Services is equipment-operations cash lent to the captive; it is a liability inside Financial Services book equity, so it is added once in the bridge as a financial asset, and its interest is excluded from the flows (matching-asset rule). Net pension/OPEB position (retirement benefit assets 3,439 vs retirement and other liabilities 1,586) is left out of the bridge and its non-cash benefit (~$0.4-0.5bn/yr) out of the flows: conservative on both sides. TIMING: FY0 is FY2026E, which ended two weeks before the valuation date, so year 1 = FY2027 and is discounted a full year; the balance sheet anchor is Q3 (2 Aug 2026), so Q4 FY2026 free cash flow (roughly $0.5-1.0bn after capex, offset by ~$0.45bn dividends plus buybacks) is not captured - a small conservative omission of about $0-2/share. BUYBACKS: Deere is an active repurchaser ($1.1bn FY2025, $0.7bn 9M FY2026, $7.2bn at the FY2023 peak), so the flat share count is funded, not a convention. CYCLE: FY2026 is management's stated trough for large ag; scenario margins are mid-cycle levels at the terminal year, not peak. No memory entry existed: first valuation of this ticker.

base.margin_note: ebitda_margin is equipment-operations adjusted EBITDA on net sales, before SBC: (segment operating profit PPA+SAT+CF less corporate other-net) + D&A + SBC. Actuals on that basis: FY2023 ~23.5%, FY2024 ~20.8%, FY2025 ~15.7% (EBIT 12.0%), FY2026E ~16.2% (9M EBIT 12.5%, includes $382m tariff recoveries against a net $502m tariff cost). 19.0% terminal = ~15.3% EBIT, in line with the FY2019-FY2026 average of ~15% and below the 20% through-cycle Leap Ambition.
base.wc_note: Negative: a manufacturer whose growth consumes inventory (19% of sales) net of payables and incentive accruals. Trade receivables are largely sold to Financial Services, so they are funded there.
base.tax_note: EO effective rate 20-23% FY2023-FY2025, 25% 9M FY2026; cash taxes ran above the provision in FY2023-FY2025. 23% held flat.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 20/50/30. Bear up to 20%: the downside is not solvency (A-rated, net financial assets in equipment operations) but a real chance that tariffs, depressed farm income and the consent decree hold margins at trough levels. Base 50%: it already assumes the cyclical recovery management is guiding to. Bull down to 30%: it needs two independent things, a strong ag upcycle and precision-ag monetisation that has repeatedly lagged Deere's own targets.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
